html:
The Cusabo were a group of Native American peoples on the coast of what is now South Carolina, from around Charleston south to the Savannah River. They included the Kiawah, Edisto, Stono, Wando, Etiwan, Combahee and Escamacu, among others.

They lived in small towns among the marshes and sea islands, farming maize and taking fish and shellfish. Europeans came early: the French built Charlesfort on Parris Island in 1562, and Spain held Santa Elena there from 1566 to 1587.

When the English founded Charles Town in 1670, the Kiawah welcomed them. The Cusabo became "Settlement Indians", living among the colonists. Disease, slave raiding and the Yamasee War of 1715 cut their numbers, and by the mid-1700s they had mostly merged into other peoples, such as the Catawba.
